summary: Point lights. On the server, Light.spawn adds a light all players see, including later joiners, until you destroy it or its resource stops, though a world export's lights stay. In a client script, only that player sees it, until destroy(), the resource stops or the world changes. Both sides check the same limits: each colour channel 0 to 1, intensity 0 to 100, radius 0.1 to 100 m. A bad value throws and changes nothing. A game shows at most 192 lights, counting both server and client ones.

id.summary: On the server, the network id. On a client, this game's own id for the light, which is not a network id.

spawn.summary: Adds a point light. On a client, it throws if the game already shows 192 script lights. Defaults are warm orange { x: 1, y: 0.6, z: 0.3 }, intensity 1, radius 5 and no shadows.

params.position: A Vector3 or { x, y, z } in metres. With `entity`, the offset from the body or joint instead, up to 8 m.
params.options: Optional: `color`, with red, green and blue in x, y and z, each 0 to 1; `intensity`, 0 to 100; `radius`, 0.1 to 100 m; `castShadows`, subject also to the game's shadow settings; `entity`, a Player or Npc to attach it to, so it follows the body in all games; `joint`, such as 'RightHand' or 'head', a joint on that body. If the body lacks the joint, it attaches to the body. In a client script only, `ambient: true` makes a room light, as the game lights its own rooms: it sets the ambient light within its radius to its colour times its intensity, without shine or shadows. Below 1 it darkens, above 1 it brightens, so one in the middle of a building, as wide as the building, warms a room the sky lights blue.

spawn.exampleLua:
local Light = kcds.world.Light
local Vector3 = kcds.math.Vector3

local lantern = Light.spawn(Vector3.new(2293.2, 2026.0, 106.5), { color = { x = 1, y = 0.55, z = 0.2 }, intensity = 2, radius = 8 })

-- A torch's glow on a player's right hand.
Light.spawn(Vector3.new(0, 0, 0.3), { entity = player, joint = "RightHand", radius = 6 })

position.summary: Its location in metres. Assign a Vector3 or { x, y, z } to move it for all players.

color.summary: Red, green and blue in x, y and z, each 0 to 1. You can assign to it.

intensity.summary: Brightness from 0, dark, to 100, as a multiplier on the colour. You can assign to it.

radius.summary: Its reach, 0.1 to 100 metres. You can assign to it.

castShadows.summary: Whether it casts shadows, false by default. It accepts only true or false, and the game's shadow settings decide whether a player sees them.

ambient.summary: Client scripts only: whether it is a room light, set by spawn's `ambient` option and read-only. A room light sets the ambient light within its radius instead of shining on surfaces.
ambient.exampleLua:
local room = kcds.world.Light.spawn(kcds.math.Vector3.new(3066, 665, 58), { ambient = true, radius = 25, color = { x = 1, y = 0.75, z = 0.5 }, intensity = 1.5 })
print("room light: " .. tostring(room.ambient))
ambient.exampleCs:
var room = Light.Spawn(new Vector3(3066, 665, 58), new { ambient = true, radius = 25, color = new { x = 1, y = 0.75, z = 0.5 }, intensity = 1.5 });
Log.Info($"room light: {room.Ambient}");

destroy.summary: Removes the light from all games. It is safe to call twice.

valid.summary: Client only. Whether the light still shines. It is false after destroy(), when its resource stopped, or when the game dropped it because of a world change or lack of room. A removed light keeps its last values for reading, and assigning does nothing.
valid.exampleLua:
-- client
local Light = kcds.world.Light
local LocalPlayer = kcds.players.LocalPlayer

local lamp = Light.spawn(LocalPlayer.position, { radius = 4 })
if not lamp.valid then
  lamp = Light.spawn(LocalPlayer.position, { radius = 4 })
end
